C715469.failed_steps: Blocked at step 4: the 2,000-line PDF cannot be judged on the QA site - its PDF service stops any PDF after 30 seconds.
C715469.source: Developer on SV-12539 (Nemanja Djuric, 11 Nov 2026, comment 80903): "Even with all the CPU QA's server has, about 1,100 rows take 42 seconds, over QA's 30-second limit … We won't change QA's setup. Please re-test PDFs between 800 and 2,000 rows on staging once this work is there."
C715469.ticket: Follow the status here https://shopview.atlassian.net/browse/SV-12539 (Open, read 12 Nov 2026).
C715469.todo: What needs to be done: run on staging once the release is there (staging allows 120 seconds per PDF). Follow the status here https://shopview.atlassian.net/browse/SV-12539 (Open, read 12 Nov 2026).
observed: Retest 12 Nov 2026 on build v26.45.3-34788b2: the same three vendors still add up to exactly 2,000 lines; the PDF stopped after 32 seconds with "We couldn't export this report. Please try again." and no file.
No new ticket: the ticket above already covers it, and the developer confirmed the QA site's 30-second PDF limit causes it (the report code does not); a second ticket would be a duplicate.

C715462.failed_steps: Blocked at step 1: an invoice paid more than its amount cannot be made - the app refuses the overpayment.
C715462.source: Production today (before the release): a payment of $1,102.93 on its $1,082.93 invoice S2-1760 is refused with "Transaction cannot be overpaid." - the same as the new build.
C715462.todo: What needs to be done: nothing to fix; this test can only run on an organization that already holds an overpaid invoice (the PRD says production has 16 such invoices, made in the past).
observed: Retest 12 Nov 2026 on build v26.45.3-34788b2: a new $100.00 invoice (S11315-17913, customer ZZX Overpaid Q13); the app's payment of $120.00 is refused with "Transaction cannot be overpaid." and the invoice stays $100.00 open. On screen (its work order's Finance page, New Payment), typing 120.00 shows "Payment cannot be higher than 100" and Make Payment stays disabled.
Production today (before the release): a payment of $1,102.93 on its $1,082.93 invoice S2-1760 is refused with "Transaction cannot be overpaid." - the same as the new build.

No new ticket: refusing an overpayment is how payments already work on production; the PRD only describes how the report treats overpaid invoices that already exist, it does not ask that new ones can be made.
